title: A small family of finite-open pairs realizes all field-valued parts
statement:
Let $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ be the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated, locally finite type morphism of $\mathcal U$-small schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exist a $\mathcal U$-small set $I$, affine $\mathcal U$-small schemes $U_i$, etale morphisms $a_i:U_i\to Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and open subschemes $W_i\subseteq X\times_YU_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion], each finite over $U_i$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with this lifting property. For every field $K$ in $\mathcal U$ [def-weil-field], map $b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$, and open subscheme $Z\subseteq X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$ finite over $K$, there exist $i\in I$, a field extension $K\hookrightarrow L$ with $L$ in $\mathcal U$, and $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to U_i$ such that
$$a_i u=b\circ\operatorname{Spec}(K\hookrightarrow L),\qquad u^*W_i=Z\times_KL$$
as open subschemes of $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}L$. Spectra and pullback use [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. The empty open part is included. No sheaf representability or algebraicity assertion is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 04QG (lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover), scheme-case proof: choices of finite unions of the split pieces and geometric-point surjectivity; preceded by the reduction of Tag 04PG (lemma-finite-lives-on-locally-quasi-finite-part). The family is restricted to one choice per finite subset of each fixed geometric fibre, then shrunk to affine neighbourhoods.

proof.text: Choose a $\mathcal U$-small family $(A_t\to Y)_{t\in T}$ of affine etale representatives using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover], applied in the universe of $Y$. This is the smallness of affine objects, not of all etale schemes: its Mathlib representative category is essentially small in precisely that universe. For each $t$, let $B_t$ be the set of opens of $X\times_YA_t$ whose restricted projection to $A_t$ is finite. Since the fibre product is $\mathcal U$-small, its opens form a subset of a power set in $\mathcal U$; so does $B_t$. By the universe closure convention [def-weil-size-convention], $I=\coprod_{t\in T}B_t$ is $\mathcal U$-small. Set $U_{(t,B)}=A_t$ and $W_{(t,B)}=B$. These pairs already have all required geometric properties; it remains to establish the lifting property.

source.place: Tag 04QG, lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover, scheme-case construction and geometric-field argument; Tag 04PG, lemma-finite-lives-on-locally-quasi-finite-part. The bounded family is obtained using the existing small affine etale representative lemma.

proof.text: Fix $(K,b,Z)$ as in the statement. Choose a $\mathcal U$-small algebraic closure $K\hookrightarrow L$ by [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique], and write $Z_L=Z\times_KL$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] it is finite over $L$. By [pqf-lem-finite-qf] and [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres], its underlying set is finite. Let $y$ be the image of $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$. The finite set of images of $|Z_L|$ in $X_y$ will be denoted $\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$. For $Z=\varnothing$ this is the empty list.

source.place: Tag 04QG, lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover, scheme-case construction and geometric-field argument; Tag 04PG, lemma-finite-lives-on-locally-quasi-finite-part. The bounded family is obtained using the existing small affine etale representative lemma.

proof.text: Let $Q\subseteq X$ be the quasi-finite locus of $f$. The locus theorem [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open], specialized to schemes, says it is open and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, including $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$. On the open $Z_L$ the base-changed map is finite and hence quasi-finite by [pqf-lem-finite-qf]; quasi-finiteness at a point is unaffected by restricting its source to an open neighbourhood. Consequently every $x_i$ belongs to $Q$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated] shows that the $x_i$ are isolated in $X_y$. Thus the local splitting lemma applies to these points of the original morphism $f$, without any global quasi-finiteness or quasi-compactness assumption.

source.place: Tag 04QG, lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover, scheme-case construction and geometric-field argument; Tag 04PG, lemma-finite-lives-on-locally-quasi-finite-part. The bounded family is obtained using the existing small affine etale representative lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-etale-splits-isolated-purely-inseparable] to $f$, $y$, and the distinct isolated points $x_i$. Obtain $(U,u)\to(Y,y)$ and $U\times_YX=W\amalg\coprod_{i,j}V_{i,j}$. Its residue extension $\kappa(u)/\kappa(y)$ is finite separable, hence algebraic. The map $\kappa(y)\to L$ determined by $b$ and $K\hookrightarrow L$ extends to an embedding $\kappa(u)\to L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed]. Composing $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ gives a lift $c$ with $a c=b\operatorname{Spec}(K\hookrightarrow L)$. In this decomposition all products are over $Y$ (the display $U\times_SX$ in the scheme-case paragraph of the source must be read as $U\times_YX$).

source.place: Tag 04QG, lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover, scheme-case construction and geometric-field argument; Tag 04PG, lemma-finite-lives-on-locally-quasi-finite-part. The bounded family is obtained using the existing small affine etale representative lemma.

proof.text: For each $(i,j)$ its special fibre $(V_{i,j})_u$ is a one-point scheme with purely inseparable residue extension over $\kappa(u)$. It is therefore radicial by [def-weil-radicial-morphism], and that node's equivalence with universal injectivity implies that its base change to $L$ has at most one point. It has a point: extend $\kappa(u)\to L$ to its algebraic residue extension $\kappa(v_{i,j})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed], and compose the resulting spectrum map with the canonical residue-field point. The fibre identification [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] identifies this scheme with $V_{i,j}\times_{U,c}\operatorname{Spec}L$. Hence each such piece has exactly one point. No reduction or identification of nonreduced schemes with their residue fields is made.

source.place: Tag 04QG, lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover, scheme-case construction and geometric-field argument; Tag 04PG, lemma-finite-lives-on-locally-quasi-finite-part. The bounded family is obtained using the existing small affine etale representative lemma.

proof.text: The pullback of $W$ to $L$ is disjoint from $Z_L$: a point of their intersection would map to one of the $x_i$, contradicting the avoidance clause of [lem-sfb-etale-splits-isolated-purely-inseparable]. Each of the other pieces has exactly one point by the preceding step. Its intersection with the open $Z_L$ is therefore either the empty open or the entire piece. Select the finite set $J$ of pieces for which it is the entire piece, and put $B=\coprod_{(i,j)\in J}V_{i,j}$ as an open of $U\times_YX$. Its projection to $U$ is finite: induct on $|J|$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct] for the binary union of disjoint pieces; for the empty union the zero algebra is generated as a module by the empty set. The two opens $c^*B$ and $Z_L$ have exactly the same points and therefore are equal as open subschemes, with their induced structure sheaves. This equality includes all nilpotent structure.

source.place: Tag 04QG, lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover, scheme-case construction and geometric-field argument; Tag 04PG, lemma-finite-lives-on-locally-quasi-finite-part. The bounded family is obtained using the existing small affine etale representative lemma.

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $U'\subseteq U$ of $u$. The map $c$ factors through $U'$ because its image is $u$. The composite $U'\to Y$ is etale by the open-immersion and composition clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Its finite open part $B'=B\times_UU'$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. Transport $(U',B',c)$ along its $Y$-isomorphism to an affine representative $A_t$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover]. The transported open belongs to $B_t$, so the corresponding $i\in I$ and transported map $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to U_i$ satisfy the two required equalities. Restriction and transport merely compose the preceding equality with pullback isomorphisms. For the empty part the chosen union is empty; if $Y$ is empty no field-valued data exist. No construction or representability of a finite-part functor has been used.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement. Reused the existing universe-small affine etale representatives and formed the small set of all their finite open parts. Proved the field-valued lifting by extending K to an algebraic closure, using the base-change-compatible quasi-finite locus to isolate the finitely many relevant ordinary fibre points, applying the new 02LO local splitting input, and selecting its one-point geometric pieces. The equality is of opens, retaining nilpotents, not just of reduced components. One statement-only local geometry node is new.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-f57b84dd8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Stacks 04PG and 04QG in full (spaces-more-groupoids.tex l.1430-1451 and l.1631-1792, scheme case plus the algebraically-closed-point argument), and more-morphisms.tex 02LM-var, 02LN and 02LO (l.12040-12160). Item statement unchanged; it is the scheme case of the 04QG datum, and the source's U x_S X correctly becomes U x_Y X. Steps checked against the cited statements. Step 1: the Mathlib leaf's match AffineEtale.instEssentiallySmall is EssentiallySmall.{u}, so the representative set is U-small; the set of finite opens is a subset of a power set, so I is U-small. Step 2: algebraic closure, finiteness by base change, finite => quasi-finite => finite fibres (pqf nodes are Lean-closed). Step 3: the 04NW locus is stable under base change, then 01TH (1)=>(2) gives isolatedness in the correct direction. Step 4: the new node's finite separable residue extension kappa(u)/kappa(y) plus 09GU gives the lift c with a c = b Spec(K->L). Step 5: radicial => universally injective gives at most one point, the 09GU extension gives one point, and fibre-of-base-change identifies the piece; matches 04QG l.1777-1781. Step 6 (elementary, justified): W avoids the x_i, each one-point piece is all-or-nothing, the finite coproduct gives B finite, and opens with the same points are equal including nilpotents. Step 7: affine shrink, etale composition, base change and transport to a representative. proof_deps = union of uses. New node lem-sfb-etale-splits-isolated-purely-inseparable matches 02LO hypothesis by hypothesis. Its additions are true: kappa(s)->kappa(u) finite separable (02GL; finite Galois in the 02LM-var proof) and kappa(v)/kappa(u) finite. Tested n=0, a rational point, a separable degree-d point (d pieces) and a purely inseparable point (one piece). It is statement-only with three kinds of search recorded. Not a duplicate: 02LM-var has no clopen W decomposition, 02LN/02LP are elementary neighbourhoods with no separable splitting, and getting 02LO from 02LM-var needs the separatedness/closedness/shrinking argument. Not a restatement of the item. Declared tool use quasi-finite-at-point-isolated (01TH generic) accepted. No SGA. Batch-5 flag on lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open (reaches def-trf-algebraic-space): accepted, because 04NW is general geometry outside the trace formula and Poincare duality and their proofs; its sec-trace-formula dependencies are only the general definition of an algebraic space and the space fibre-product node, and the parent is already about algebraic spaces.
